scientific_model.concept: Knowledge Distillation with Temperature: Soft Targets and the T² Factor
scientific_model.purpose: Explain how a teacher's logits are turned into soft targets by a temperature-scaled softmax, how the student's soft-target cross-entropy is computed, and why the soft-loss term is multiplied by T² when combined with a hard-label loss.
scientific_model.focus_alignment: Section 2: explain knowledge distillation with small teacher and student logit vectors and adjustable temperature. Show the soft probability distributions and the soft-target cross-entropy or a clearly labeled component of it. Explain the temperature effect and the T-squared factor when combining soft and hard training losses. Do not train models.

variables.meaning: Logits of the cumbersome teacher model for one transfer case.
Logits of the distilled student model for the same transfer case.
Softmax temperature used both to generate the teacher's soft targets and to train the student.
One-hot correct-label distribution over the same classes, used for the hard cross-entropy at T = 1.
Weight on the hard-label cross-entropy relative to the T²-scaled soft-target term.
Teacher logits divided by T, then softmaxed, giving the soft target distribution p_i = e^{v_i/T} / Σ_j e^{v_j/T}.
Student logits divided by the same T, then softmaxed, giving q_i = e^{z_i/T} / Σ_j e^{z_j/T}.
Soft-target cross-entropy H(p,q) = -Σ_i p_i ln q_i in nats, computed at the same temperature T used to make the soft targets.
The same student logits softmaxed at temperature 1, as used for the hard-label cross-entropy.
Hard-label cross-entropy H(y, q^(1)) = -Σ_i y_i ln q_i^(1) in nats, computed at temperature 1.
Weighted combination: the soft-target cross-entropy is multiplied by T² to compensate the 1/T² gradient scaling, and the hard-label cross-entropy is weighted by α.

assumptions: One transfer case is shown; the paper averages such per-case losses over the transfer set.
The hard-label distribution is a one-hot vector over the same class index used for the teacher's target class.
limitations: We compute the loss components, not the gradients dC/dz_i; the 1/T² gradient scaling is cited but not derived here.
The T² factor is applied as a fixed multiplier on the soft cross-entropy term; the paper's argument is about gradient magnitudes, and we do not re-derive it from the gradient expression.
misconceptions: That temperature changes the teacher's knowledge or the class ranking. Temperature only rescales logits before softmax; it changes the sharpness of the distribution, not the ordering of classes.
edge_cases: T = 1 makes the soft distribution equal to the ordinary softmax and removes the T² rescaling effect (T² = 1).
A very large T drives both distributions toward uniform, so the soft cross-entropy approaches ln(K) and carries little class-specific signal.
scientific_model.demonstration_scope: A single transfer case with small fixed teacher and student logit vectors. We compute the temperature-scaled softmax distributions, the soft-target cross-entropy component, and the T²-scaled combination with a hard-label cross-entropy. No model training, no gradient derivation, no multi-example averaging.

lesson_spec.central_learning_question: Explain how a teacher's logits are turned into soft targets by a temperature-scaled softmax, how the student's soft-target cross-entropy is computed, and why the soft-loss term is multiplied by T² when combined with a hard-label loss.
learning_objectives: Compute teacher and student softmax distributions at a chosen temperature T and interpret how T controls their sharpness.
Compute the soft-target cross-entropy H(p_T, q_T) and the T²-scaled combination with a hard-label cross-entropy.
audience_prerequisites: Softmax as a normalized exponential of logits.
Cross-entropy H(p,q) = -Σ p_i ln q_i in nats.
lesson_spec.intuition: A high softmax temperature flattens the teacher's distribution, exposing relative preferences among non-target classes that a hard label hides. The student is trained to match this soft distribution. Because raising T shrinks the soft-loss gradients by roughly 1/T², the soft term is multiplied by T² so that its influence relative to the hard-label term stays comparable when T is changed.

guided_explorations.title: Low temperature sharpens the soft targets
guided_explorations.observe: Calculated results for this setup, compared with the starting inputs: p (teacher soft targets) = [0.86681333, 0.11731043, 0.01587624] (starting value: [0.66524096, 0.24472847, 0.090030573]); q (student soft predictions) = [0.73612472, 0.16425163, 0.099623648] (starting value: [0.54340561, 0.25668664, 0.19990775]); H(p, q) = 0.51407383 nats (starting value: 0.88347618 nats); q^(1) (student at T = 1) = [0.73612472, 0.16425163, 0.099623648] (starting value: [0.73612472, 0.16425163, 0.099623648]); H(y, q^(1)) = 0.30635571 nats (starting value: 0.30635571 nats); L = 0.60598055 nats (starting value: 3.6258114 nats).
guided_explorations.why: Dividing logits by a smaller T preserves larger gaps between logits, so the softmax is sharper; the soft cross-entropy then depends mostly on the top class, and the T² rescaling is inactive.

guided_explorations.title: High temperature softens the targets and amplifies the soft term
guided_explorations.observe: Calculated results for this setup, compared with the starting inputs: p (teacher soft targets) = [0.44844086, 0.32132192, 0.23023722] (starting value: [0.66524096, 0.24472847, 0.090030573]); q (student soft predictions) = [0.40074826, 0.31210306, 0.28714868] (starting value: [0.54340561, 0.25668664, 0.19990775]); H(p, q) = 1.071498 nats (starting value: 0.88347618 nats); q^(1) (student at T = 1) = [0.73612472, 0.16425163, 0.099623648] (starting value: [0.73612472, 0.16425163, 0.099623648]); H(y, q^(1)) = 0.30635571 nats (starting value: 0.30635571 nats); L = 38.665836 nats (starting value: 3.6258114 nats).
guided_explorations.why: Dividing logits by a large T compresses their differences, so softmax approaches uniform and the soft targets carry less class-specific signal; the T² factor grows quadratically, compensating the 1/T² gradient scaling so the soft term's relative influence stays comparable when T is tuned.
